title: Hopeverse: Car Chase v2 (heartbeat chase)
maker: ElevenLabs Music API on the owner's paid plan

request.prompt: Breathless car chase film score cue, composed and played like a real film composer's action cue, not a DJ mix and not a generic old action BGM. The core idea: the listener's HEARTBEAT is the rhythm. A deep, close, physical heartbeat 'lub-dub' on a felt kick and low taiko is the spine of the whole track, and the main tune is phrased to lock onto every heartbeat, so the heart and the melody race together. It starts at a nervous heartbeat, then the heartbeat speeds up and doubles into a racing pulse at a true full 160 BPM drive, never half-time; the drums and a sixteenth-note string and veena ostinato run on top of the racing heartbeat. E minor. Signature sounds: the car's own sounds as instruments: a deep engine rev tuned to the root as the growling bass drone that rises in pitch as the car accelerates, gear-shift clunks as snare accents, a tyre screech tuned into a short lead stab, the ticking indicator as the hi-hat; plus a glitch-chopped veena riff and pitched-down mridangam hits. Signature motif: a rising 3-note call (root, up a minor third, up to the fifth, the last note held and bent upward) on a gritty synth lead in the first 5 seconds and again at the end. 0-8 s: silence-close heartbeat alone, slow and nervous, the engine idling on the root, the 3-note call. 8-12 s: the heartbeat speeds up bar by bar, the engine revs with it, a drummer's pickup fill, one reversed veena swell into the first big hit. 12-28 s: the chase: racing heartbeat pulse at full speed, the bold 4-bar brass and synth theme phrased exactly on the heartbeats, sixteenth-note strings and veena racing, tyre-screech stabs answering each phrase. 28-30 s: the near miss: everything cuts to the pounding heartbeat alone for two beats and a gasp of breath, then the band slams back in. 30-46 s: the second chase, up a whole step, the heartbeat even harder, the theme varied and climbing, a strings counter-melody, call-and-response shouts 'hey!'. 46-56 s: the climax, everything at full power, the heartbeat and the tune hitting together on every downbeat. 56-60 s: the escape: one final hit, the heartbeat slows down to calm, and the 3-note call rings out alone on the veena. Something new happens at least every 8 seconds; the drive never drops in the middle. No white-noise risers or filter sweeps, no build-and-drop, no EDM drops, no stutters, no side-chain pumping, no DJ transitions; clear, tonal, punchy cinematic mix.

brief.notes: Jithesh 29 Oct on v1: take A has no real chase part 'where the heartbeat goes with the tune'; take B sounds like old BGMs. v2: a heartbeat pulse is the rhythmic spine, the tune locks to it, true full-tempo drive, no half-time.

story: A high-speed car chase through a night city, from ignition to the final escape.
human_work: to be added by the owner: melody, take choice, edits, mix
